9: # Crashlytics
10: 
11: This skill provides a complete guide for getting started with Crashlytics on
12: Android or iOS. Crash data collected from client applications can be read using
13: the MCP server in the Firebase CLI.
14: 
15: ## Prerequisites
16: 
17: Provisioning Crashlytics requires both a Firebase project and a Firebase app,
18: either Android or iOS. To read the data collected by Crashlytics, install the
19: MCP server in the Firebase CLI. See the `firebase-basics` skill for references.
20: 
21: ## SDK Setup
22: 
23: To learn how to setup Crashlytics in your application code, choose your
24: platform:
25: 
26: - **Android**: [android_setup.md](references/android_setup.md)
27: - **iOS**: [ios_setup.md](references/ios_setup.md)
28: 
29: ## SDK Usage
30: 
31: The SDK provides a number of features to make crash reports more actionable.
32: 
33: - Add custom keys
34: - Add custom logs
35: - Set user identifiers
36: - Report non-fatal exceptions
37: 
38: To learn how to customize crash reports and add additional debugging data,
39: consult the documentation for your platform.
40: 
41: - **Android**:
42:   [Customize Crash Reports for Android](https://firebase.google.com/docs/crashlytics/android/customize-crash-reports.md)
43: - **iOS**:
44:   [Customize Crash Reports for Apple Platforms](https://firebase.google.com/docs/crashlytics/ios/customize-crash-reports.md)", "references/android_setup.md": "1: # Firebase Crashlytics Android Setup Guide

8: ## Project and App Setup
9: 
10: Before you begin, ensure you have the following. If a `google-services.json`
11: file is present, then use that Firebase project and app. Otherwise you may need
12: to create them.
13: 
14: - **Firebase CLI**: Installed and logged in (see `firebase-basics`).
15: - **Firebase Project**: Created via
16:   `npx -y firebase-tools@latest projects:create` (see `firebase-basics`).
17: - **Firebase App**: Created via
18:   `npx -y firebase-tools@latest apps:create <IOS|ANDROID|WEB> <package-name-or-bundle-id>`
19: 
20: The `google-services.json` file must be present in the Android app's module
21: directory. If missing, get the config using the Firebase CLI:
22: `npx -y firebase-tools@latest apps:sdkconfig ANDROID <App-ID>`.
23: 
24: ## Add Dependencies to Gradle Build
25: 
26: These changes are made to your Android project's Gradle files.
27: 
28: ### Project-level `build.gradle.kts` (`<project>/build.gradle.kts`)
29: 
30: Add the latest version of the Crashlytics Gradle plugin to the `plugins` block.
31: Fetch the
32: [latest version from the Google Maven repository](https://maven.google.com/web/index.html?q=firebase-crashlytics-gradle#com.google.firebase:firebase-crashlytics-gradle)
33: before adding this.
34: 
35: ```kotlin
36: plugins {
37:     // ... other plugins
38:     id("com.google.firebase.crashlytics") version "<latest_plugin_version>" apply false
39: }
40: ```
41: 
42: ### App-level `build.gradle.kts` (`<project>/<app-module>/build.gradle.kts`)
43: 
44: 1. Add the Crashlytics plugin to the `plugins` block:
45: 
46:    ```kotlin
47:    plugins {
48:        // ... other plugins
49:        id("com.google.firebase.crashlytics")
50:    }
51:    ```
52: 
53: 1. Add the Firebase Crashlytics dependency to the `dependencies` block. It is
54:    recommended to use the Firebase Bill of Materials (BoM) to manage SDK
55:    versions. Fetch the
56:    [latest version from the Google Maven repository](https://maven.google.com/web/index.html?q=firebase-bom#com.google.firebase:firebase-bom)
57:    before adding this.
58: 
59:    ```kotlin
60:    dependencies {
61:        // ... other dependencies
62: 
63:        // Import the Firebase BoM
64:        implementation(platform("com.google.firebase:firebase-bom:<latest_bom_version>"))
65: 
66:        // Add the dependencies for the Crashlytics and Analytics
67:        implementation("com.google.firebase:firebase-crashlytics-ktx")
68:    }
69:    ```
70: 
71: ## Follow up Steps
72: 
73: ### Optional: Install the NDK SDK to capture native crashes
74: 
75: If your app uses native code (C/C++), or includes a library with native code,
76: you can configure Crashlytics to report native crashes.
77: 
78: App-level `build.gradle.kts` (`<project>/<app-module>/build.gradle.kts`)
79: 
80: 1. Add the `firebase-crashlytics-ndk` dependency:
81: 
82:    ```kotlin
83:    dependencies {
84:        // ... other dependencies
85:        implementation("com.google.firebase:firebase-crashlytics-ndk:18.6.2")
86:    }
87:    ```
88: 
89: 1. Enable the `nativeSymbolUpload` flag in your `buildTypes` configuration. This
90:    will automatically upload symbol files for your native code, which are
91:    required to symbolicate native crash reports.
92: 
93:    ```kotlin
94:    android {
95:        // ... other config
96:        buildTypes {
97:            getByName("release") {
98:                // ...
99:                firebaseCrashlytics {
100:                    nativeSymbolUploadEnabled = true
101:                }
102:            }
103:        }
104:    }
105:    ```
106: 
107: After these changes, Crashlytics will automatically report crashes in your app's
108: native code.
109: 
110: ### Required: Force a Test Crash
111: 
112: To verify that Crashlytics is correctly installed, you need to force a test
113: crash in the app.
114: 
115: 1. Add code to your main activity (e.g., in `onCreate`) to trigger a crash a few
116:    seconds after app startup:
117: 
118:    ```kotlin
119:    import android.os.Handler
120:    import android.os.Looper
121: 
122:    // ... in your Activity's onCreate method or similar startup logic
123:    Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).postDelayed({
124:        throw RuntimeException("Test Crash") // Force a crash after 3 seconds
125:    }, 3000)
126:    ```
127: 
128: 1. Run your app on a device or emulator. The app should crash after a short
129:    delay.
130: 
131: 1. Restart the app. The Crashlytics SDK will send the crash report to Firebase
132:    on the next app launch.
133: 
134: 1. After a few minutes, the crash should be available in the Firebase console.
135:    Go to **DevOps & Engagement** > **Crashlytics** to view your dashboard and
136:    crash reports.
137: 
138: - If the Firebase MCP server is installed, use the `get_report` tool to check
139:   that a crash was received.
140: - As a fallback, visit the Crashlytics dashboard in the Firebase console to see
141:   the new crash report.
142: 
143: 5. After verifying that Firebase has received the crash report - either using
144:    the `get_report` tool or manually viewing it in the Firebase console - remove
145:    the code from step 1 that triggers the crash. This prevents the application
146:    from always crashing on start up after a delay.
147: 
148: ### Optional: Add custom debugging information
149: 
150: Customize reports to help you better understand what's happening in your app and
151: the circumstances around events reported to Crashlytics. See
152: [Customize Crash Reports for Android](https://firebase.google.com/docs/crashlytics/android/customize-crash-reports.md).", "references/ios_setup.md": "1: # Firebase Crashlytics iOS Setup Guide

9: ## Project and App Setup
10: 
11: Use the `firebase-tools` CLI to set up the project if necessary.
12: 
13: 1. **Find Bundle ID:** Read the Xcode project to find the iOS bundle ID. Check
14:    the `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` value in the `.pbxproj` file or the
15:    `Info.plist` file.
16: 1. **Create Firebase Project:** If no project exists, create one:
17:    `npx -y firebase-tools@latest projects:create <project-id> --display-name="My Awesome App"`
18: 1. **Create Firebase App:** Register the iOS app with the discovered bundle ID:
19:    `npx -y firebase-tools@latest apps:create IOS <bundle-id>`
20: 1. **Link the GoogleService-Info.plist file:** Use the script in the
21:    `xcode-project-setup` skill to obtain the config and link.
22: 
23: ## Add Swift Package Dependencies
24: 
25: Install the Crashlytics SDK using the Swift package manager, or the script in
26: the `xcode-project-setup` skill.
27: 
28: Install the `FirebaseCrashlytics` package from the
29: `https://github.com/firebase/firebase-ios-sdk.git` repository.
30: 
31: ## Initialize Firebase in App Code
32: 
33: Modify the application's entry point to initialize Firebase. Refer to the iOS
34: setup reference in the `firebase-basics` skill.
35: 
36: ## Add dSYM Upload Script
37: 
38: Add a Run Script phase to the main app target in Xcode. This step is required to
39: upload dSYM files for crash symbolication.
40: 
41: 1. **Debug Information Format**: The `Debug Information Format` in Build
42:    Settings must be set to `DWARF with dSYM File`.
43: 1. **Run Script Content**: A new "Run Script Phase" should be added to the
44:    target's "Build Phases" with the following content:
45:    ```bash
46:    ${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/firebase-ios-sdk/Crashlytics/run
47:    ```
48: 
49: When using the `xcode-project-setup` skills, the above two steps will be done as
50: part of adding the `FirebaseCrashlytics` package. Once the skill has been
51: invoked and succeeded, verify that the app's project.pbxproj file contains a Run
52: Script Build phase where the shell script attribute value contains
53: 'Crashlytics'. Specifically, there should be a `PBXShellScriptBuildPhase`
54: section with the attribute `shellScript` that is set to a value that contains
55: `Crashlytics/run` and an attribute `inputPaths` where one of the values contains
56: `GoogleService-Info.plist`. If verification is not successful, present the above
57: two options to be done manually.
58: 
59: ## Follow up Steps
60: 
61: ### Required: Force a Test Crash
62: 
63: 1. Add code to trigger a crash a few seconds after app startup to verify
64:    Crashlytics setup.
65: 
66: **For SwiftUI Apps (in `AppDelegate.swift`):**
67: 
68: ````
69: *File: `AppDelegate.swift`*
70: ```swift
71: import FirebaseCore
72: import Dispatch // For DispatchQueue
73: 
74: // ...
75: 
76: class AppDelegate: NSObject, UIApplicationDelegate {
77:   func application(_ application: UIApplication,
78:                    didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey : Any]? = nil) -> Bool {
79:     FirebaseApp.configure()
80:     // Force a crash after a delay to test Crashlytics
81:     DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) {
82:         fatalError("Test Crash")
83:     }
84:     return true
85:   }
86: }
87: ```
88: ````
89: 
90: 2. Run your app on a device or simulator. If running in the iOS simulator, make
91:    sure that the Xcode debugger is disconnected, otherwise the crash will not
92:    make it to Crashlytics. The app should crash after a short delay.
93: 
94: 1. Restart the app. The Crashlytics SDK will send the crash report to Firebase
95:    on the next app launch.
96: 
97: 1. After a few minutes, the crash should be available in the Firebase console.
98:    Go to **DevOps & Engagement** > **Crashlytics** to view your dashboard and
99:    crash reports.
100: 
101: - If the Firebase MCP server is installed, use the `get_report` tool to check
102:   that a crash was received.
103: - As a fallback, visit the Crashlytics dashboard in the Firebase console to see
104:   the new crash report.
105: 
106: 5. After verifying that Firebase has received the crash report - either using
107:    the `get_report` tool or manually viewing it in the Firebase console - remove
108:    the code from step 1 that triggers the crash. This prevents the application
109:    from always crashing on start up after a delay.
110: 
111: ### Optional: Add custom debugging information
112: 
113: Customize reports to help you better understand what's happening in your app and
114: the circumstances around events reported to Crashlytics. See
115: [Customize Crash Reports for Apple Platforms](https://firebase.google.com/docs/crashlytics/ios/customize-crash-reports.md)."}}
